newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HUNT LASCARIS, JUPITER SHARE TOP S.AFRICAN AD SPOT.
newsitem.headline: HUNT LASCARIS, JUPITER SHARE TOP S.AFRICAN AD SPOT.

text.p: South Africa's first international advertising agency Hunt Lascaris TBWA and rising star the Jupiter Group jointly won the country's leading advertising award for 1996/97.

The Financial Mail, announcing the winner of its Agency of the Year award, said no other candidates possessed the required balance of growth and creativity, among other factors, to qualify in the way the two winners did.
Jupiter won in the agency growth category, by swelling its income in 1996 by 76 percent compared to Hunt Lascaris' 43 percent income growth.

"During the past year, the Jupiter Group has made the transition from a medium-sized to a large agency, and from a focused advertising group to a diverse group of marketing communications companies," the FM said.
It added that Jupiter's income growth was higher than any other of the top 20 agencies in South Africa, making it the 10th largest agency from its previous 16th position.
But Hunt Lascaris defeated Jupiter in creative awards, snatching 7,372 points to Jupiter's 4,628 points.

"Hunt's creative score was the highest since points have been tallied in this way, but in relation to its size Jupiter scored higher. It won more than twice as many creative points per rand of billing than Hunt Lascaris," the FM said.

The FM said that if Hunt Lascaris continued its current growth trend it would likely overtake South Africa's biggest agency Ogilvy & Mather Rightford, pushing aside contender Lindsay Smithers-FCB in the process.
Hunt Lascaris became South Africa's first international agency when it joined forces with TBWA, an international agency which now holds a majority stake in Hunt lascaris TBWA.
The category of large agencies comprises those with 150 million rand minimum gross client billings.
